rationale.paradigm_idiomaticity: State is threaded through pure predicates and foldl/4 drives the insert and delete sequences; there is no assert/retract. Dispatch uses if-then-else inside single clauses (insert_key, ins_nonfull, del_internal, fix_child) rather than clause-head matching. The first clause of del/4 uses a red cut with select/3. In del/4 the clause order and the cut in clause 2 make leaf versus internal dispatch depend on ordering. Predicates are mostly deterministic and functional, but they follow an imperative 'compute indices, then replace_nth' style. Clause-head pattern matching on key position, and splitting the nodes into separate clauses, would earn one more point.
rationale.language_idiomaticity: The code uses nth0/4 in both insert and delete modes, foldl/4, append/3, select/3, memberchk, last/2 and length/2 as generators. It reimplements a few things: count_less is a hand-written recursion, which is not tail-recursive, and replace_nth is a thin wrapper over nth0/4. Naming is conventional (snake_case) and the comments are in the expected form. One departure is rot_right, which uses append(LKs0,[LKm],LKs) to take the last element where last/2 or append would be more explicit. Overall it is solid SWI-Prolog.
rationale.readability: Predicates are small and named after CLRS operations (split_child, fix_child, rot_right, merge_left). Mode comments appear on some predicates but not all, and the index arithmetic (I1, I2, NI) is dense. del_internal and ins_nonfull are long, with nested if-then-else. The insert_key comment on the root split is missing; split_child is used with parent keys [] and children [R0], a trick that needs explanation. A decent comment block exists at the top. Splitting the long predicates and adding mode docs would improve it.
rationale.design: The decomposition is sensible: membership check, split, insertion into a non-full node, and deletion split into del, del_internal and fix_child, with four small rotation and merge helpers. split_child is shared by root and child splitting. Structural duplication remains: rot_left and rot_right, and merge_left and merge_right, are near-mirror copies, and the membership check is repeated at each level. Data are plain lists with nth0 index access (O(T) per node), which meets the complexity bound. A cleaner design would use list-splitting helpers or a view of the node as left/separator/right.

anti_patterns: if-then-else chains inside single clauses instead of clause-head pattern matching
index-based access with nth0/replace_nth throughout, in an imperative style
red cut in del/4 to separate leaf, key-present and descend cases
hand-rolled count_less instead of a library predicate (partition or take_while style)
justification: The solution is pure, uses foldl/4 for the key sequences, and passes state explicitly with no assert. It is organised around the CLRS operations. However, much of the control flow is if-then-else inside single clauses, and the index-driven nth0/replace_nth style makes it feel imperative. A red cut orders the clauses of del/4, and the mirrored rotation and merge predicates duplicate logic, so it lands in the middle of the range.
